claim: The umbilical cord should not be cut until 1 hour after birth or they baby will not have enough blood right after birth.
justification: The Claim is refuted because high-confidence evidence from authoritative sources like the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) and the World Health Organization (WHO) recommends umbilical cord clamping delays of 30-60 seconds to 1-3 minutes, not 1 hour. Evidence also shows that cutting the cord before 1 hour does not cause immediate blood insufficiency in healthy newborns, though it may increase the risk of anemia later in infancy.
